claim: G-quadruplex (G4) DNA structures have been suggested to play a role in chromosomal looping.
source: Although the role of G-quadruplex (G4) DNA structures has been suggested in chromosomal looping this was not tested directly.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as background information without specific supporting data in this manuscript, indicating it draws from prior literature.

claim: An array of G4s was inserted within chromatin in cells to test causal function.
source: Here, to test causal function, an array of G4s, or control sequence that does not form G4s, were inserted within chromatin in cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental design and methods used to insert G4 arrays.

claim: In vivo G4 formation of the inserted G4 sequence array was confirmed using G4-selective antibody.
source: In vivo G4 formation of the inserted G4 sequence array, and not the control sequence, was confirmed using G4-selective antibody.
evidence: BG4 antibody ChIP-qPCR data is presented in the manuscript showing G4 formation.

claim: The control sequence did not form G4s in vivo.
source: In vivo G4 formation of the inserted G4 sequence array, and not the control sequence, was confirmed using G4-selective antibody.
evidence: BG4 antibody ChIP-qPCR data shows lack of G4 formation in the control sequence.

claim: There was a remarkable increase in the number of 3D chromatin looping interactions from the inserted G4 array compared to the control insert.
source: Compared to the control insert, we observed a remarkable increase in the number of 3D chromatin looping interactions from the inserted G4 array.
evidence: Hi-C data presented in the manuscript shows increased interactions from the G4 array.

claim: The increase in 3D chromatin looping interactions was evident within the immediate topologically associated domain (TAD).
source: This was evident within the immediate topologically associated domain (TAD) and throughout the genome.
evidence: Hi-C analysis shows interactions within the TAD containing the insertion site.

claim: The increase in 3D chromatin looping interactions was evident throughout the genome.
source: This was evident within the immediate topologically associated domain (TAD) and throughout the genome.
evidence: Circos plots and genome-wide Hi-C contact analysis demonstrate interactions across the genome.

claim: Recruitment of enhancer histone marks increased in the G4-array locally.
source: Locally, recruitment of enhancer histone marks and the transcriptional coactivator p300/Acetylated-p300 increased in the G4-array, but not in the control insertion.
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac shows increased levels at the G4 insertion site.

claim: Recruitment of the transcriptional coactivator p300/Acetylated-p300 increased in the G4-array locally.
source: Locally, recruitment of enhancer histone marks and the transcriptional coactivator p300/Acetylated-p300 increased in the G4-array, but not in the control insertion.
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for p300 and acetylated p300/CBP shows increased recruitment at the G4 insertion site.

claim: Enhancer histone marks did not increase in the control insertion.
source: Locally, recruitment of enhancer histone marks and the transcriptional coactivator p300/Acetylated-p300 increased in the G4-array, but not in the control insertion.
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data comparing G4-array to G4-mutated control shows no increase in the control.

claim: Promoter-enhancer interactions were clear up to 5 Mb away from the insertion site.
source: Resulting promoter-enhancer interactions and gene activation were clear up to 5 Mb away from the insertion site.
evidence: Gene expression data and 3C data show effects on genes up to 5 Mb from the insertion site.

claim: Gene activation was clear up to 5 Mb away from the insertion site.
source: Resulting promoter-enhancer interactions and gene activation were clear up to 5 Mb away from the insertion site.
evidence: mRNA expression data shows increased expression of genes up to 5 Mb from the insertion site.

claim: G4s have a causal role in enhancer function.
source: Together, these show the causal role of G4s in enhancer function and long-range chromatin interactions.
evidence: The experimental design with G4 insertion and control, combined with ChIP and expression data, supports causality.

claim: G4s have a causal role in long-range chromatin interactions.
source: Together, these show the causal role of G4s in enhancer function and long-range chromatin interactions.
evidence: Hi-C data showing increased interactions specifically from the G4 array supports causality.

claim: Mechanisms of 3D topology are primarily based on DNA-bound architectural proteins that induce/stabilize long-range interactions.
source: Mechanisms of 3D topology are primarily based on DNA-bound architectural proteins that induce/stabilize long-range interactions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: The underlying intrinsic DNA sequence/structure is involved in 3D looping.
source: Involvement of the underlying intrinsic DNA sequence/structure in 3D looping shown here therefore throws new light on how long-range chromosomal interactions might be induced or maintained.
evidence: The experimental results showing G4 structure effects on looping support this claim.

claim: G4s were primarily observed to be able to regulate gene expression when present around transcription start sites (TSSs).
source: G4s were primarily observed to be able to regulate gene expression when present around transcription start sites (TSSs; Huppert and Balasubramanian, 2007; Rawal et al., 2006; Verma et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: G4s can regulate gene expression by directly regulating recruitment of transcription factors and RNA polymerase.
source: G4s can regulate gene expression by directly regulating recruitment of transcription factors and RNA polymerase or via alteration of DNA accessibility by modulating the epigenetic state of the gene promoters (Hussain et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2011; Lago et al., 2021; Mukherjee et al., 2019; Saha et al., 2017; Sharma et al., 2021; Varshney et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: G4s can regulate gene expression via alteration of DNA accessibility by modulating the epigenetic state of the gene promoters.
source: G4s can regulate gene expression by directly regulating recruitment of transcription factors and RNA polymerase or via alteration of DNA accessibility by modulating the epigenetic state of the gene promoters (Hussain et al., 2017; Kumar et al., 2011; Lago et al., 2021; Mukherjee et al., 2019; Saha et al., 2017; Sharma et al., 2021; Varshney et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Recent studies have implicated the role of G4s in long-distance gene regulation.
source: Recent studies have implicated the role of G4s in long-distance gene regulation (Robinson et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: High-throughput chromosome conformation capture techniques reveal that specific regions of the human genome interact in three dimensions (3D) via chromatin looping and formation of topologically associated domains (TADs).
source: High-throughput chromosome conformation capture techniques reveal that specific regions of the human genome interact in three dimensions (3D) via chromatin looping and formation of topologically associated domains (TADs; Bonev and Cavalli, 2016; Denker and de Laat, 2016; Roy et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature describing established methods and findings.

claim: Recent computational studies observed enrichment of G4s in TAD boundaries along with higher enrichment of architectural proteins like CTCF and cohesin.
source: Interestingly, recent computational studies observed enrichment of G4s in TAD boundaries along with higher enrichment of architectural proteins like CTCF and cohesin (Hou et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior computational studies.

claim: Multiple studies noted the presence of G4s correlated with enhancer histone marks like H3K27Ac and H3K4Me1.
source: Further, multiple studies noted the presence of G4s correlated with enhancer histone marks like H3K27Ac and H3K4Me1, and predominantly open chromatin regions (Calo and Wysocka, 2013; Hou et al., 2021; Shlyueva et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: G4s are correlated with predominantly open chromatin regions.
source: Further, multiple studies noted the presence of G4s correlated with enhancer histone marks like H3K27Ac and H3K4Me1, and predominantly open chromatin regions (Calo and Wysocka, 2013; Hou et al., 2021; Shlyueva et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: A region near the 79 millionth position of chromosome 12 was markedly isolated with little or no interaction with its surrounding regions.
source: We looked into Hi-C data from Rao et al., 2014 and identified a region that was markedly isolated with little or no interaction with its surrounding regions (as shown by snapshots of Hi-C interaction matrices obtained using the 3D genome browser Wang et al., 2018 in Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of published Hi-C data and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The region near chr12:79872423–79872424 was devoid of any G4s in the vicinity (no G4 forming motifs in a±2.5 kb window).
source: In addition, this region was devoid of any G4s in the vicinity (no G4 forming motifs in a±2.5 kb window).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of the genomic sequence.

claim: An array of G4 forming sequences (275 bp long) was artificially inserted at chr12:79872423–79872424 using CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing.
source: Thereafter, we artificially inserted an array of G4 forming sequences (275 bp long) at this region near the 79 millionth position of chromosome 12 (79M in following text, chr12:79872423–79872424, hg19 genome assembly) using CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The experimental procedure is described and shown in figures.

claim: A control sequence of identical length was inserted in HEK293T cells at the same locus where specific G/Cs necessary for G4 formation were substituted so that G4s are not formed by this sequence.
source: To study specific effects due to G4s, if any, a control sequence of identical length was inserted in HEK293T cells at the same locus where specific G/Cs necessary for G4 formation were substituted so that G4s are not formed by this sequence (G4-mutated control, Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The experimental design and control sequence are described and shown in figures.

claim: The GC content was minimally affected by the substitutions in the control sequence (72.4% from 76.73%).
source: we also ensured that the GC content was minimally affected by the substitutions (72.4% from 76.73%).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the control construct.

claim: Homozygous insertion was confirmed by PCR using primers adjacent to the insertion site followed by Sanger sequencing.
source: Homozygous insertion was confirmed by PCR using primers adjacent to the insertion site followed by Sanger sequencing (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: PCR and sequencing data are presented in the figures.

claim: The array of G4-forming sequences used for insertion was previously reported to form stable G4s in human cells.
source: The array of G4-forming sequences used for insertion was previously reported to form stable G4s in human cells (Lim et al., 2010; Monsen et al., 2020; Palumbo et al., 2009; Sharma et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Significant BG4 binding was clear in the G4-array insert.
source: Significant BG4 binding was clear in the G4-array insert, and not in the G4-mutated insert, demonstrating formation of G4s by the inserted G4-array (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: BG4 ChIP-qPCR data is presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: BG4 binding was not detected in the G4-mutated insert.
source: Significant BG4 binding was clear in the G4-array insert, and not in the G4-mutated insert, demonstrating formation of G4s by the inserted G4-array (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: BG4 ChIP-qPCR data is presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was a significant increase in H3K4Me1 in the G4-array when compared to the G4-mutated control.
source: We observed significant increase in H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer marks in the G4-array when compared to the G4-mutated control (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K4Me1 is presented in Figure 2A.

claim: There was a significant increase in H3K27Ac in the G4-array when compared to the G4-mutated control.
source: We observed significant increase in H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer marks in the G4-array when compared to the G4-mutated control (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K27Ac is presented in Figure 2B.

claim: There was no G4-specific change in the presence of chromatin compaction mark H3K27Me3.
source: However, there was no G4-specific change in the presence of chromatin compaction marks, H3K27Me3 and H3K9Me3, or the promoter activation mark H3K4Me3 (Figure 2C, D and E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K27Me3 is presented in Figure 2C.

claim: There was no G4-specific change in the presence of chromatin compaction mark H3K9Me3.
source: However, there was no G4-specific change in the presence of chromatin compaction marks, H3K27Me3 and H3K9Me3, or the promoter activation mark H3K4Me3 (Figure 2C, D and E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K9Me3 is presented in Figure 2D.

claim: There was no G4-specific change in the promoter activation mark H3K4Me3.
source: However, there was no G4-specific change in the presence of chromatin compaction marks, H3K27Me3 and H3K9Me3, or the promoter activation mark H3K4Me3 (Figure 2C, D and E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K4Me3 is presented in Figure 2E.

claim: H3K4Me1 is associated with enhancers.
source: The G4-dependent recruitment of H3K4Me1 (associated with enhancers Heintzman et al., 2009; Heintzman et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: H3K27Ac is associated with active enhancers and promoters.
source: and H3K27Ac (associated with active enhancers and promoters Creyghton et al., 2010; Heintzman et al., 2009; Heintzman et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The G4-dependent recruitment of H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac indicated enhancer-like characteristics of the inserted G4s.
source: The G4-dependent recruitment of H3K4Me1 (associated with enhancers Heintzman et al., 2009; Heintzman et al., 2007) and H3K27Ac (associated with active enhancers and promoters Creyghton et al., 2010; Heintzman et al., 2009; Heintzman et al., 2007) indicated enhancer-like characteristics of the inserted G4s.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ChIP data and established knowledge about histone marks.

claim: The expression of PAWR increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells.
source: Notably, the expression of four of the tested genes (PAWR, PPP1R12A, NAV3, and SLC6A15) increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: mRNA expression data is presented in Figure 3A.

claim: The expression of PPP1R12A increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells.
source: Notably, the expression of four of the tested genes (PAWR, PPP1R12A, NAV3, and SLC6A15) increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: mRNA expression data is presented in Figure 3A.

claim: The expression of NAV3 increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells.
source: Notably, the expression of four of the tested genes (PAWR, PPP1R12A, NAV3, and SLC6A15) increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: mRNA expression data is presented in Figure 3A.

claim: The expression of SLC6A15 increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells.
source: Notably, the expression of four of the tested genes (PAWR, PPP1R12A, NAV3, and SLC6A15) increased in the G4-array insert compared to the mutated insert control cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: mRNA expression data is presented in Figure 3A.

claim: There was a concomitant increase in the recruitment of Ser5 phosphorylated RNA Pol II in the surrounding gene promoters.
source: Based on this enhanced expression, we further tested and observed a somewhat concomitant increase in the recruitment of Ser5 phosphorylated RNA Pol II in the surrounding gene promoters (Figure 3B).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for Pol2 Phospho-Ser5 is presented in Figure 3B.

claim: There was a G4-dependent increase in chromosomal looping interactions of the insertion locus with the gene promoters.
source: The 3C assays revealed that there was a G4-dependent increase in chromosomal looping interactions of the insertion locus with the gene promoters (Figure 3C).
evidence: 3C assay data is presented in Figure 3C.

claim: The inserted G4-array sequence was acting like an enhancer element.
source: These results suggested that the inserted G4-array sequence was acting like an enhancer element.
evidence: This is an inference based on the histone marks, gene expression, and looping data.

claim: There was a relatively modest increase in the recruitment of p300 within the G4-array when compared against the mutated control.
source: There was a relatively modest increase in the recruitment of p300, and a more substantial increase in the recruitment of the more functionally active acetylated p300/CBP, was seen within the G4-array when compared against the mutated control (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for p300 is presented in Figure 3D.

claim: There was a more substantial increase in the recruitment of the more functionally active acetylated p300/CBP within the G4-array when compared against the mutated control.
source: There was a relatively modest increase in the recruitment of p300, and a more substantial increase in the recruitment of the more functionally active acetylated p300/CBP, was seen within the G4-array when compared against the mutated control (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for acetylated p300/CBP is presented in Figure 3E.

claim: p300 is a transcriptional coactivator.
source: To understand the mechanism behind the enhancer-like property of the inserted G4-array we analyzed the recruitment of transcriptional coactivator p300 (Kalkhoven, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: There was a significant decrease in the expression of PPP1R12A when the G4 array inserted cells were treated with the G4 targeting LNAs.
source: We observed that there was a significant decrease in the expression of PPP1R12A and NAV3, two of the genes initially observed to have G4-dependent enhanced expression (Figure 3A), when the G4 array inserted cells were treated with the G4 targeting LNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: mRNA expression data after LNA treatment is presented in Figure 4B.

claim: There was a significant decrease in the expression of NAV3 when the G4 array inserted cells were treated with the G4 targeting LNAs.
source: We observed that there was a significant decrease in the expression of PPP1R12A and NAV3, two of the genes initially observed to have G4-dependent enhanced expression (Figure 3A), when the G4 array inserted cells were treated with the G4 targeting LNAs (Figure 4B).
evidence: mRNA expression data after LNA treatment is presented in Figure 4B.

claim: A decrease in the H3K4Me1 enhancer histone modification was evident within the insert upon the LNAs treatment.
source: As expected, although modest, a decrease in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer histone modifications was evident within the insert upon the LNAs treatment (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K4Me1 after LNA treatment is presented in Figure 4C.

claim: A decrease in the H3K27Ac enhancer histone modification was evident within the insert upon the LNAs treatment.
source: As expected, although modest, a decrease in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer histone modifications was evident within the insert upon the LNAs treatment (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K27Ac after LNA treatment is presented in Figure 4D.

claim: Changes in the expression of the genes were not significant across replicates in case of G4-mutated insert cells upon LNA treatment.
source: Changes in the expression of the genes were not significant across replicates in case of G4-mutated insert cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Data is presented in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The disruption of the inserted G4s can reverse the enhancer functions observed upon G4 insertion.
source: These indicate that the disruption of the inserted G4s can reverse the enhancer functions observed upon G4 insertion, further supporting the role of the G4 structure in enhancer functions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the LNA treatment experiments.

claim: The G4-inserted locus had more than twice as many genome-wide Hi-C interactions compared to the mutated control (6390 vs 3133).
source: Compared to the mutated control, the G4-inserted locus had more than twice as many genome-wide Hi-C interactions (6390 vs 3133; Figure 5A and B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Hi-C contact data is presented in Figure 5 and Supplementary file 1.

claim: After normalizing for sequencing depth, the number of Hi-C contacts from the same window in HEK293T was relatively similar to the G4-mutated insert control (3968 and 3133 respectively).
source: After normalizing for sequencing depth, the number of Hi-C contacts from the same window in HEK293T was relatively similar to the G4-mutated insert control (3968 and 3133 respectively, Figure 5C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Hi-C contact data is presented in Figure 5C and Supplementary file 1.

claim: A significant number of new long-range interactions were induced throughout the genome due to the inserted G4s.
source: Together, these showed that a significant number of new long-range interactions were induced throughout the genome due to the inserted G4s, but not from the inserted control sequence.
evidence: This is based on the Hi-C data comparing G4-array to controls.

claim: The inserted control sequence did not induce new long-range interactions throughout the genome.
source: Together, these showed that a significant number of new long-range interactions were induced throughout the genome due to the inserted G4s, but not from the inserted control sequence.
evidence: This is based on the Hi-C data comparing G4-array to controls.

claim: The number of Hi-C interactions in the G4-array insert was clearly enriched compared to the G4-mutated insert control.
source: The number of Hi-C interactions in the G4-array insert was clearly enriched compared to the G4-mutated insert control, as expected from the global Hi-C contacts noted above.
evidence: This is based on analysis of Hi-C matrices shown in Figure 6.

claim: The insertion per se did not affect the overall domain architecture.
source: We noted that while the interactions from the G4-array insert were significantly more, the insertion per se did not affect the overall domain architecture, which was largely similar between G4 or G4-mutated inserts as clear from Figure 6A and B.
evidence: Hi-C matrices in Figure 6A and B show similar domain structures.

claim: The chromatin domain architecture remained relatively unchanged on introducing the G-array or G4-mutated regions.
source: Comparison using reported HiC data for the same region from HEK293T cells showed this to be the case confirming that the chromatin domain architecture remained relatively unchanged on introducing the G-array or G4-mutated regions (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Comparison with HEK293T Hi-C data is shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The G4-array induced significantly more Hi-C interactions particularly in the downstream regions.
source: This clearly showed that the G4-array induced significantly more Hi-C interactions; interestingly this was particularly evident in the downstream regions.
evidence: This is based on the differential Hi-C heatmap shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The number of interactions with the G4-array insertion region was significantly enhanced in the downstream region relative to the upstream.
source: When we plotted the significantly different chromosomal interactions with minimum 20 interaction reads, it was again clear that the number of interactions with the G4-array insertion region was significantly enhanced in the downstream region relative to the upstream (Figure 6F).
evidence: Interaction data is shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The insertion of G4s induced long-range interactions with minimal organizational changes in the 3D chromatin domain.
source: Overall, these support that the insertion of G4s induced long-range interactions with minimal organizational changes in the 3D chromatin domain, underlining the molecular role of G4s in the arrangement of 3D chromatin.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Hi-C data showing increased interactions but preserved TAD structure.

claim: The site of insertion was very close and downstream to the TAD boundary.
source: A close look at the Hi-C contact matrices indicated that the site of insertion was very close and downstream to the TAD boundary (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is based on visual inspection of Hi-C matrices in Figure 6A-C.

claim: The G4-dependent long-range interactions were largely within the TAD, and limited in the upstream region due to the TAD boundary.
source: We reasoned that the G4-dependent long-range interactions were largely within the TAD, and limited in the upstream region due to the TAD boundary.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Hi-C data and the position of the insertion relative to the TAD boundary.

claim: The inserted G4 array had enhanced Hi-C interactions across the domain, prominently featured in the downstream regions.
source: This is clearly seen in Figure 6C, akin to an 'architectural stripe' displaying that the inserted G4 array had enhanced Hi-C interactions across the domain, thus prominently featured in the downstream regions.
evidence: This is based on the Hi-C differential heatmap in Figure 6C.

claim: A relative increase in the H3K4Me1 enhancer mark in the G4-array at the 10M locus was evident compared to the G4-mutated control.
source: A relative increase in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer marks in the G4-array was evident compared to the G4-mutated control (Figure 7C and D), consistent with earlier observations following G4 insertion at the 79 M locus (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K4Me1 at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7C.

claim: A relative increase in the H3K27Ac enhancer mark in the G4-array at the 10M locus was evident compared to the G4-mutated control.
source: A relative increase in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer marks in the G4-array was evident compared to the G4-mutated control (Figure 7C and D), consistent with earlier observations following G4 insertion at the 79 M locus (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K27Ac at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7D.

claim: The enhanced levels of H3K27Ac at the 10M locus were not as marked as the 79 M locus.
source: We noticed, however, that the enhanced levels of H3K27Ac were not as marked as the 79 M locus.
evidence: This is based on comparison of ChIP-qPCR data between the two loci.

claim: There was a relative increase in the H3K27Me3 repressor mark at the 10M locus compared to the control mutated-G4 insert, particularly at the downstream end of the insertion locus.
source: On the other hand, interestingly, relative increase in the H3K27Me3 repressor mark compared to the control mutated-G4 insert, particularly at the downstream end of the insertion locus was seen (Figure 7E).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K27Me3 at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7E.

claim: There was no G4-specific change in the presence of the chromatin compaction mark H3K9Me3 at the 10M locus.
source: There was no G4-specific change in the presence of the chromatin compaction mark H3K9Me3, or the promoter activation mark H3K4Me3 (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K9Me3 at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7F.

claim: There was no G4-specific change in the promoter activation mark H3K4Me3 at the 10M locus.
source: There was no G4-specific change in the presence of the chromatin compaction mark H3K9Me3, or the promoter activation mark H3K4Me3 (Figure 7F and G).
evidence: ChIP-qPCR data for H3K4Me3 at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7G.

claim: There was a G4-dependent increase in the expression of KLRC2 at the 10M locus.
source: As expected from earlier observations and the enhancer histone marks, there was a G4-dependent increase in the expression of surrounding genes KLRC2, KLRC1 and NTF3; except for PTPRO, which had reduced expression (Figure 7H).
evidence: mRNA expression data at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7H.

claim: There was a G4-dependent increase in the expression of KLRC1 at the 10M locus.
source: As expected from earlier observations and the enhancer histone marks, there was a G4-dependent increase in the expression of surrounding genes KLRC2, KLRC1 and NTF3; except for PTPRO, which had reduced expression (Figure 7H).
evidence: mRNA expression data at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7H.

claim: There was a G4-dependent increase in the expression of NTF3 at the 10M locus.
source: As expected from earlier observations and the enhancer histone marks, there was a G4-dependent increase in the expression of surrounding genes KLRC2, KLRC1 and NTF3; except for PTPRO, which had reduced expression (Figure 7H).
evidence: mRNA expression data at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7H.

claim: PTPRO had reduced expression at the 10M locus.
source: As expected from earlier observations and the enhancer histone marks, there was a G4-dependent increase in the expression of surrounding genes KLRC2, KLRC1 and NTF3; except for PTPRO, which had reduced expression (Figure 7H).
evidence: mRNA expression data at the 10M locus is presented in Figure 7H.

claim: The presence of the H3K27Me3 repressor histone mark, along with H3K27Ac/H3K4Me1 enhancer histone marks, indicates a poised enhancer-like state.
source: Notable variations however must be pointed out: like the presence of the H3K27Me3 repressor histone mark, along with H3K27Ac/H3K4Me1 enhancer histone marks, indicating a poised enhancer-like state as described earlier (Calo and Wysocka, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the histone mark data and supported by a citation.

claim: The impact of G4 formation on chromatin is likely context-specific, dependent on the chromatin state of the adjacent regions.
source: These suggest the impact of G4 formation on chromatin is likely context-specific, that is, dependent on the chromatin state of the adjacent regions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differences observed between the 79M and 10M insertion sites.

claim: Hi-C experiments showed an enhanced number of cis- and trans-chromosomal long-range interactions emanating from the introduced G4s.
source: To directly test if G4s affect long-range chromatin organization we artificially inserted an array of G4s in the chromatin. Hi-C experiments clearly showed an enhanced number of cis- and trans-chromosomal long-range interactions emanating from the introduced G4s.
evidence: This is based on the Hi-C data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Most new long-range interactions following G4 incorporation were downstream from the site of insertion.
source: Furthermore, interestingly, most new long-range interactions following G4 incorporation were downstream from the site of insertion.
evidence: This is based on the Hi-C data analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: The G4 insertion locus was proximal to the upstream TAD boundary thereby restricting most new interactions to the downstream regions within the TAD.
source: This is likely because the G4 insertion locus was proximal to the upstream TAD boundary thereby restricting most new interactions to the downstream regions within the TAD (Figures 5 and 6).
evidence: This is an inference based on the Hi-C data and TAD structure analysis.

claim: The insertion of the G4 array led to enhanced expression of genes up to 5 Mb away compared to cells with the G4 mutated control insertion.
source: The insertion of the G4 array led to enhanced expression of genes up to 5 Mb away compared to cells with the G4 mutated control insertion.
evidence: This is based on the gene expression data presented in Figure 3A.

claim: There was enrichment in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer histone marks at the G4 insertion site.
source: Furthermore, there was enrichment in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer histone marks, along with recruitment of transcriptional coactivator p300 and more prominently the functionally active acetylated p300/CBP.
evidence: This is based on the ChIP-qPCR data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: There was recruitment of transcriptional coactivator p300 at the G4 insertion site.
source: Furthermore, there was enrichment in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer histone marks, along with recruitment of transcriptional coactivator p300 and more prominently the functionally active acetylated p300/CBP.
evidence: This is based on the ChIP-qPCR data presented in Figure 3D.

claim: There was recruitment of the functionally active acetylated p300/CBP at the G4 insertion site.
source: Furthermore, there was enrichment in the H3K4Me1 and H3K27Ac enhancer histone marks, along with recruitment of transcriptional coactivator p300 and more prominently the functionally active acetylated p300/CBP.
evidence: This is based on the ChIP-qPCR data presented in Figure 3E.

claim: The enhancer marks were relatively reduced when the inserted G4s were specifically disrupted.
source: The enhancer marks were relatively reduced, although not markedly, when the inserted G4s were specifically disrupted (Figure 4).
evidence: This is based on the LNA treatment experiments shown in Figure 4.

claim: The enhancer-like effects observed upon G4 insertion at the 79 M locus were largely replicated when the same G4-array was inserted in another locus (10 M).
source: The enhancer-like effects observed upon G4 insertion at the 79 M locus were largely replicated when the same G4-array was inserted in another locus (10 M).
evidence: This is based on comparison of data from both insertion sites presented in Figures 2 and 7.

claim: The G4-dependent increase in H3K27Me3 at the 10 M locus, in addition to the enhancer mark H3K4Me1, supports formation of a poised enhancer-like state.
source: Interestingly, the G4-dependent increase in H3K27Me3 at the 10 M locus, in addition to the enhancer mark H3K4Me1, supports formation of a poised enhacer-like state, as described earlier (Calo and Wysocka, 2013).
evidence: This is an inference based on the histone mark data at the 10M locus and supported by a citation.

claim: Both the inserted G4 regions induced enhancer-like chromatin.
source: Although both the inserted G4 regions induced enhancer-like chromatin, notable context-specific influence, likely due to the chromatin-state at the regions adjacent to the insertion locus, were evident.
evidence: This is based on comparison of data from both insertion sites.

claim: Findings directly support the function of G4s as enhancer-like elements.
source: Taken together, findings here directly support the function of G4s as enhancer-like elements and as factors that enhance long-range chromatin interactions.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Findings directly support the function of G4s as factors that enhance long-range chromatin interactions.
source: Taken together, findings here directly support the function of G4s as enhancer-like elements and as factors that enhance long-range chromatin interactions.
evidence: This is a summary inference based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Such interactions are possibly contextually dependent on the type of G4 structure, in addition to the adjacent sequence context.
source: It is possible that such interactions are also contextually dependent on the type of G4 structure, in addition to the adjacent sequence context, and further studies will be necessary to elucidate these.
evidence: This is speculation about future research directions.

claim: The inserted sequence was from the hTERT promoter region with multiple arrayed G4s.
source: First, we introduced an array of G4s and confirmed in vivo G4 formation; the inserted sequence was from the hTERT promoter region with multiple arrayed G4s (Lim et al., 2010; Monsen et al., 2020; Palumbo et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes the source of the inserted sequence and is supported by citations.

claim: The selected insertion locus was otherwise devoid of intrinsic G4s in a±2.5 kb window.
source: Second, we selected an insertion locus that was otherwise devoid of intrinsic G4s in a±2.5 kb window.
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for the insertion site.

claim: The selected insertion locus was relatively sparse in long-range interactions.
source: Third, the selected insertion locus was relatively sparse in long-range interactions.
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for the insertion site based on Hi-C data.

claim: The impacts of mutations in the control sequence on the binding of specific transcription factors associated with the sequence, particularly SP1, cannot be ruled out.
source: Although the introduced mutations for the control sequences were minimal, the impacts of such mutations on the binding of specific transcription factors associated with the sequence, particularly SP1, reported to bind G4s (Raiber et al., 2012), cannot be ruled out.
evidence: This is a caveat about potential confounding factors, supported by a citation.

claim: Promoter G4s are involved in regulating gene expression.
source: Existing literature shows promoter G4s are involved in regulating gene expression (Huppert and Balasubramanian, 2007; Rawal et al., 2006; Verma et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: G4s have been reported to regulate chromatin epigenetics through both cytosine methylation and histone modifications.
source: Additionally, G4s have been reported to regulate chromatin epigenetics through both cytosine methylation and histone modifications (Halder et al., 2010; Mao et al., 2018; Sengupta et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Promoter G4s regulate gene expression by recruiting histone-modifying regulatory complexes.
source: Previous studies by us further show that promoter G4s regulate gene expression by recruiting histone-modifying regulatory complexes (Hussain et al., 2017; Mukherjee et al., 2019; Saha et al., 2017; Sharma et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies by the authors.

claim: CTCF was observed to bind to G4s.
source: CTCF, an architectural protein primarily involved in TAD boundary formation, was observed to bind to G4s and G4 stabilization was noted to enhance CTCF occupancy (Tikhonova et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: G4 stabilization was noted to enhance CTCF occupancy.
source: CTCF, an architectural protein primarily involved in TAD boundary formation, was observed to bind to G4s and G4 stabilization was noted to enhance CTCF occupancy (Tikhonova et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: G4s were noted to be enriched in TAD boundaries and associated with the formation of chromatin loops.
source: In addition, G4s were noted to be enriched in TAD boundaries and associated with the formation of chromatin loops (Hou et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: G4s were found to coincide with open chromatin regions and H3K27Ac and H3K4Me1 ChIP-Seq peaks, which are markers for transcriptional enhancers.
source: G4s were also found to coincide with open chromatin regions and H3K27Ac and H3K4Me1 ChIP-Seq peaks, which are markers for transcriptional enhancers (Calo and Wysocka, 2013; Hou et al., 2021; Lyu et al., 2022; Shlyueva et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Most G4-containing regions were observed to overlap with annotated enhancers.
source: Most of these regions were observed to overlap with annotated enhancers and promoters regulated by such enhancers were enriched in G4s (Williams et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Promoters regulated by G4-containing enhancers were enriched in G4s.
source: Most of these regions were observed to overlap with annotated enhancers and promoters regulated by such enhancers were enriched in G4s (Williams et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: A recent G4 CUT&Tag study noted G4 formation at both active promoters and active and poised enhancers.
source: A recent G4 CUT&Tag study further noted G4 formation at both active promoters and active and poised enhancers (Lyu et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: It was proposed that inter-molecular G4 formation between distant stretches of Gs may lead to DNA looping.
source: Further, it was proposed that inter-molecular G4 formation between distant stretches of Gs may lead to DNA looping (Hegyi, 2015; Liano et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Promoters of PAWR, PPP1R12A, NAV3 and SLC6A15 harbor potential G4-forming sequences (pG4).
source: Consistent with this, we noted with interest promoters of the four genes (PAWR, PPP1R12A, NAV3 and SLC6A15; Figure 3A), activated on long-range interaction with the inserted loci, harbor potential G4-forming sequences (pG4) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Relative enrichment in pG4s was evident within the significantly enhanced contact points.
source: Relative enrichment in pG4s was evident, particularly within the significantly enhanced contact points, at times spreading beyond the interacting region (Figure 6F, lower panel).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: The YY1 transcription factor was found to bind to G4s.
source: The YY1 transcription factor was found to bind to G4s and dimerization of G4-bound YY1 led to chromatin looping interactions and consequent regulation of target gene expression (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Dimerization of G4-bound YY1 led to chromatin looping interactions and consequent regulation of target gene expression.
source: The YY1 transcription factor was found to bind to G4s and dimerization of G4-bound YY1 led to chromatin looping interactions and consequent regulation of target gene expression (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: R-loops and possibly R-loop-associated G4 formation are enriched at CTCF binding sites.
source: A recent study also showed R-loops and possibly R-loop-associated G4 formation are enriched at CTCF binding sites, and stronger CTCF binding facilitated by G4s promotes chromatin looping (Wulfridge et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Stronger CTCF binding facilitated by G4s promotes chromatin looping.
source: A recent study also showed R-loops and possibly R-loop-associated G4 formation are enriched at CTCF binding sites, and stronger CTCF binding facilitated by G4s promotes chromatin looping (Wulfridge et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: G4s assist in RNA polymerase II-associated chromatin looping.
source: In addition, it was shown that G4s assist in RNA polymerase II-associated chromatin looping (Yuan et al., 2023).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Findings demonstrate a causal role of G4s in inducing both long-range associations and enhancer function.
source: In summary, our findings here demonstrate a causal role of G4s in inducing both long-range associations and enhancer function.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the experimental data.

claim: Findings from a G4-forming stretch inserted at two independent loci illustrate the function of G4s in 3D gene regulation.
source: Findings from a G4-forming stretch inserted at two independent loci illustrate the function of G4s in 3D gene regulation.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experiments at both insertion sites.

claim: DNA secondary structure motifs directly control the state of 3D chromatin.
source: Together these shed new mechanistic light on how DNA secondary structure motifs directly control the state of 3D chromatin and thereby biological function.
